column1: # Known original bugs and deliberate port deviations.
# One row per finding. This is the index a QoL pass works from: every bug the port reproduces is
# here, with the address the evidence came from and where the reproduction lives in the port.
# kind        bug        the original does something wrong
#             residue    the return value is whatever a register happened to hold
#             missing    the original has no test it should have (not-found, out-of-range, no floor)
#             naming     the IDA name describes the function wrongly; behaviour is fine
#             duplicate  the original contains the same function twice
#             deviation  the port deliberately differs from the original
# reproduced  yes   the port reproduces it, and a test asserts it
#             no    the port does NOT reproduce it (a deviation), listed here so it is not lost
#             n/a   the original function is not ported yet
# qol         yes   a QoL patch should probably fix this
#             no    fixing it would change intended game behaviour
# Port-side bugs we introduced and fixed are NOT listed here; they are recorded in docs/parity/.

column4: what_the_original_does
column5: evidence

column4: The hangar marker byte is written into the facility block numbered by Ship.bCraftType, not Ship.bHomeBase. The three grid reads in the same scan use bHomeBase. A type 1 craft landing at base 3 writes into base 1's grid.
column5: MUL R2,R3,R8 at 0x68588 where R3 is Ship.bCraftType; the reads scale by 24*bHomeBase

column4: Base_UpdateStoresNeeded is called with (i8)(2 * ship index) as its base index, not the base being processed. Ship 1 updates base 2; ship 4 names base 8, past the eight base blocks.
column5: MOV R3,R8,LSL#24 / MOV R9,R3,ASR#24 / MOV R1,R9; R8 last written at 0x68654 as 2*shipIdx from the ship-index stack slot

column4: The manufacturing quantity column at 0x15E19C is shifted one base LATER than every other per-base array. Product B and product C land on column idx-1; this one lands on idx. The removed base keeps its manufacturing values.
column5: Fixed offsets 16756 versus 12404 and 5604 against the same 400/800-byte column stride

column4: The facility-type search has no found test. A type no base has leaves the index on the base count, the compaction guard fails, and the function still drops the count and deletes apBases[count-1] - so it removes the LAST base.
column5: Loop exit at 0x66BB0, guard at 0x66E4C, unconditional delete at 0x6715C

column4: When no strateg entry matches, the index equals the item count and StrategList_RemoveAt is called one past the end.
column5: Search loop at 0x66BE4, call at 0x66C58

column4: The argument is used with two meanings in one function: a facility type at 0x66BB8 and a SITE ID at 0x66BE4. Not a bug, but it is why the name is misleading.
column5: 0x66BB8 compares nFacType, 0x66BE4 compares StrategItem.nSiteId

column4: No found test. The search loop ends with the index at the count and 0x36BE0 deletes apSoldiers[count], one slot past the array, and decrements the count anyway.
column5: 0x36BE0 store against the loop-exit index

column4: Removing items while walking forward skips entries, so a purge pass does not remove everything it should.
column5: Forward walk against a shrinking array

column4: Only subtracts when the byte is already non-zero, but has no floor: 30 minus 40 becomes 246. It also does not check the found index, so it can touch abGrid[-1].
column5: 0x6ACEC body

column4: Returns the constant 1620, which is whatever R0 happened to hold.
column5: 0x6ACEC return

column4: No sentinel test on the craft index, so asking for craft 255 counts the soldiers who are aboard nothing.
column5: 0x6649C compares bUnk183 against the argument with no bound

column4: Charges 50,000 per month for every facility cell whose TYPE byte is not 255, and never checks build days. An unfinished facility is charged the full amount, the opposite of every capacity function in the same family.
column5: 0x6A230 reads the type grid only

column4: The original contains the same search twice: 0x5A8D0 and 0x6AC30 search BaseRec.bUnk4 and return -1, differing only in bounds. The port keeps one implementation and deliberately does not cite 0x5A8D0.
column5: 0x5A8D0 versus 0x6AC30

column4: The name says it clears a grid row. It clears nothing: it classifies a base and stores a state byte into 0x161F38.
column5: 0x6A0E0 body

column4: Returns 6 no matter what it did: the inner counter is reset to 0 on every row and always runs to 6. It also calls Base_CalcWorkshopCap at 0x65BC0 and discards the result.
column5: 0x65C20 reset, 0x65BC0 discarded call

column4: The unit-removal bound is re-read from nCivilianUnitCount / nXcomUnitCount on every iteration while the index keeps advancing, so the walk can skip entries against a shrinking list.
column5: 0x3DD0C loop, bound reload at 0x3DD40 and 0x3DDFC

column4: Slot 34 is asymmetric: the base is charged 5 per unit and the craft is credited 50. The same asymmetry appears on the landing path at 0x68948, so it is the game's rule rather than a hangar-screen quirk - listed because it looks like a bug and a QoL pass will be asked about it.
column5: 0x7AC38 and 0x68948

column4: The original falls back to a rolled v124.dat read when the primary read fails. The port reproduces the roll but not the file-level retry, because the port's asset reader has no equivalent.
column5: 0x44248 fallback branch

column4: The original resolves the palette as 0x1472D0 + 256 * (Map.paletteBase + slot), where paletteBase is a dword read out of the Map block. The port indexes g_aPalette[(nPal + 0) & (PUFO_PAL_SLOTS - 1)] - the +0 is a placeholder for that Map-resident base, which the port does not model yet.
column5: 0x9EC48 decompile, palette index expression

column4: Every 5-6-5 field is scaled with (f * key) >> 8. With key = 255 that is (f * 255) >> 8, which is f - 1 for every non-zero field, so a fully opaque blend still loses one unit in red, green and blue. dst 0xFFFF blended with colour 0xFFFF at key 255 gives 0xF7DE, never 0xFFFF.
column5: 0xA460C blend expression; test_render asserts 0xF7DE

column4: nKey = 0 does not mean "leave the destination alone". The inverse factor is 255 - 0 = 255, so the existing pixel is scaled by 255/256 and every non-zero field drops by one. dst 0x001F with key 0 becomes 0x001E.
column5: 0xA4590 computes 255 - nKey before the loop; test_render asserts 0x001E

column4: The original stores the transparency index in a global (blitColorKey @ 0xa3028) that SoftSurf_BlitIndexedKeyed_Inner reads for every glyph byte. The port keeps the setter but its keyed blit takes the key as a parameter, so nothing in the port reads the stored value.
column5: 0xA3728 and 0xA3840 load blitColorKey and BEQ past the write on a glyph-byte match

column4: The bounds test is x <= nSurf0 and y <= nSurf1, not <. A coordinate equal to the dimension is accepted: sampling at x == width reads the first pixel of the next row, and at y == height it reads past the end of the surface buffer.
column5: 0xA4630 bounds compares; test_render asserts SamplePixel(4,0) on a 4-wide surface returns the next row's pixel

column4: The same 420-byte body appears twice in the original, at 0xa3a14 as Blit_CopyRows and at 0xa3db8 as SoftSurf_BlitCopyRaw: same three pixel-mode branches, same loop bodies. The port keeps one implementation and cites both addresses.
column5: Both decompilations are identical line for line; both are 420 bytes in docs/idb/inventory-grouped.tsv

column4: The 24bpp branch writes three bytes per pixel (LDRH/STRH then LDRB/STRB) but advances the destination by only two (ADD R7,R7,#2), while the row step at 0xa3614 is 3 * nSurf0. Pixels overlap each other and a row of n of them covers 2n bytes of a 3n-byte row.
column5: Disassembly at 0xa35e4; test_render asserts the second pixel starts at +2 and that byte 5 of the row is never written

column4: Named SoftSurf_BlitIndexed_Mode12 in the IDB although nothing in it indexes a palette: it copies the glyph's own pixel values into the loaded surface. Renamed in the IDB to SoftSurf_BlitRawGlyph. IDA reports no cross-references to it, and the same is true of SoftSurf_BlitCopyRaw @ 0xa3db8 and SoftSurf_SamplePixel @ 0xa4630.
column5: set_type and rename applied in the IDB; xrefs_to 0xa33c8 returns none

column4: The character index is var34[v41 + v34], where v34 is the line number. Line 0 draws from character 0, line 1 from character 1, line 2 from character 2 - each line drops as many leading characters as its own index, even though each line is a different 205-byte text record. With the count formula (cursor - line - 1) the result is a diagonal reveal, not a typewriter.
column5: 0x26E14 loads v35[v41 + v34]; the loop at 0x26EF0 advances the record pointer by 205 per line while v34 also increments

column4: The right border strip is drawn at nX + nWidth, one pixel outside the body the fill just covered, while the left border sits at nX. The dialog frame is therefore one pixel wider on the right than the filled area.
column5: 0x265D4 blits at v9 + nWidth where v9 = (240 - nWidth)/2 and the fill at 0x26538 covers nWidth from v9

column4: The original copies a text record into a 92-byte stack buffer (var34[92]) with no length check, so a record longer than 91 characters corrupts the stack. The port uses a 205-byte buffer, the full record size.
column5: var34[92] at bp-34h; the copy loop at 0x26DB0 runs until the terminator with no bound

column4: Ten text records are copied one after another into the caller's scratch buffer by byte loops with no length check, so a long record corrupts whatever follows it. The port uses PUFO_TEXT_REC_STRIDE, the full record size.
column5: copy loops at 0x20F44, 0x20F98, 0x21008, 0x2107C, 0x210CC, 0x21104, 0x21140, 0x21178, 0x211B0 and 0x211EC all write through pIso->szText with no bound

column4: The action-latch switch handles modes 2, 3 and 4 and sends every other value above 1 to the draw with nGlyphA never assigned, so the marker is drawn with whatever glyph index the previously drawn cell left in the shared context. Mode 0 and 1 take a defined path; 5 and above do not.
column5: default branch at 0x1B324 goes to LABEL_27, and the only writes to pIso->nGlyphA before it are at 0x1B384 (mode 3) and 0x1B40C

column4: Same shape in the high marker: an action-latch value that is not 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 jumps straight to the draw with a stale nGlyphA and nGlyphB left at zero.
column5: goto LABEL_35 at 0x1B608

column4: The gate tests the whole dword at Map+0x14000 while the glyph index reads the same place with LDRH. A value that is only non-zero in the high half passes the gate and then contributes nothing to the index, so the glyph drawn is the one the low half alone selects.
column5: Gate at 0x1C2B4 is a dword load, the index at 0x1C674 uses LDRH R3, [R7, R12]

column4: The mode 1 team rule loads the selected base byte with LDRSB and compares it against Soldier.nKind, which is an unsigned byte. A base byte of 0x80 or more sign-extends to a negative int and then matches no nKind at all, so the tactical roster comes out empty. Base indices are small in practice, so the quirk is latent.
column5: LDRSB R2, [R1, R12] at 0x398B0 loads unk_159D81; CMP R3, R2 then compares it against LDRB R3, [R0, #0xB6]

column4: The 24-bit branch reads HIBYTE(w) and the low byte of w, so it only ever sees the low 16 bits of a palette entry, and it writes back a 16-bit value. Palette_Load packs the 0x100 format as R | G<<8 | B<<16, so on a 24-bit display this pass drops the whole blue channel out of every palette. Harmless on the 16bpp devices the game shipped on, which is probably why it survived.
column5: ARM at 0x37718 uses HIBYTE(v5) and at 0x37760 (u8)v5; the store at 0x377BC writes the repacked 16-bit value back over the 4-byte slot

column4: operator new is not checked. The null is stored into Map.apSoldiers at 0x22BF0 and dereferenced on the next instruction at 0x22C10, so a failed allocation is a crash rather than a behaviour. There is also no bounds check on the roster array; the index is the low half of a u16 count.
column5: No test between 0x22BC0 and 0x22C10. apSoldiers[LOWORD(nSoldierCount)] written at 0x22BF0, then [count]->nUnk440 at 0x22C10

column4: The roster is freed with operator delete without nulling the slots and without clearing the count. If FindChunk or the 2-byte count read fails, nSoldierCount still names memory that has already been freed, and the next pass through the roster frees it again.
column5: Free loop at 0x430FC writes nothing back; the only early exits are 0x43124 and 0x4313C, both after the free loop

column4: The third pickup stores the selected unit, the hit item and the pointer position, but unlike the two slot passes (0x3BF38, 0x3C1D8) and the ammo pickup (0x3C3EC) it never zeroes nInvDragOffX/Y. It inherits the footprint offset the previous re-test left, so a 2-wide item picked up just before leaves -20, the re-test lands at 150,150 which is inside no hit rect at all, and the slot it was aiming at is missed.
column5: 0x3C4C8 writes pSelUnit, 0x3C4D0 writes pInvHitItem, 0x3C4DC and 0x3C4EC write the pointer from aInvHitRects[10]; there is no store to Map+0x4A28 or Map+0x4A2C anywhere in that block

column4: The slot ammo swap is unreachable. The branch is entered only when nIndex != abUnk1012[slot] (0x3BF9C), and the match at 0x3C000 needs nIndex == abUnk1012[slot] with the same two operands. So the second walk always runs to the end of the list and changes nothing.
column5: 0x3BF9C is CMP R3,R2 / BEQ loc_3C110 with R3 = i->nIndex and R2 = abUnk1012[slot]; 0x3C000 is CMP R3,R2 / BEQ loc_3C0F0 with the same pair

column4: auStat[8] is the divisor of the carry gate and is reached through __rt_sdiv with no zero test, so a soldier with strength 0 divides by zero. auStat[8] is loaded with LDRH, so it is the unsigned 16-bit stat, and abUnk1012 is a byte array while TactItem.nIndex is a u16, making the compare 16-bit against 8-bit.
column5: 0x3C280 LDRH R0,[R7,#0xB2] then 0x3C298 LDR R3,=_rt_sdiv / MOV PC,R3

column4: When the last soldier in the roster has nUnitType 6, which is the soldier object index 33 just created, the loop skips its ammo computation and writes nAmmo = 0 into apTactItems[nTactItemCount]: a slot this iteration has not created yet. In shipped memory that slot is whatever the pointer array holds past the count.
column5: ARM 0x39A14 is LDRH count / ADD R3,R5,R3,LSL#2 / LDR R3,[R3,#0x1194] / LDRB R3,[R3,#0xA0] / CMP R3,#6; 0x39A5C stores 0 through apTactItems[Map_nTactItemCount] and jumps to the shared tail at 0x39B20

column4: The hardware ammo switch has cases 31, 32, 34 and 35 with default: break, so object index 33 never assigns the ammo total. The split at the end of the copy loop then reuses whatever total the previous object index left, so hardware soldiers from object 33 carry the wrong clip size.
column5: 0x39A68 is the switch; 0x39B20 is the default break that every path converges on; 0x39D50 and 0x39D98 read the same stack slot var_C that only cases 31, 32, 34 and 35 write

column4: The fourth race group's count is read from stack slot var_24, which the function never writes. The group it bounds is the one that gets Map_abSpriteSet[3], so the fourth sprite set is handed out based on whatever a previous frame left at SP+0x6C.
column5: var_24 has exactly two references in the whole 3516-byte function: the frame declaration and this LDR. The bound it feeds is CMP R7, (var_24 + var_28 + var_2C + var_30) at 0x3A8CC, and the group body at 0x3A8DC loads Map_abSpriteSet+3

column4: The alien set index is stored for mission mode 0, 1, 2 and 3 but the BNE at 0x3A2F0 leaves the slot unwritten for any mode above 3, and that index then selects a row of the eight-row composition table and of the eight-entry mission totals table.
column5: 0x3A31C (mode 0), 0x3A30C (mode 1), 0x3A304 (mode 2) and 0x3A2F4 (mode 3, R2 preloaded to 5) all store it; 0x3A2F0 is the fall-through that stores nothing; 0x3A338 overwrites it when nMissionType is 9

column4: nPal is saved on the stack at entry and zeroed when the unit is operative, but only the paths that pass the visibility gate write it back. A small operative unit on an unflagged cell, and a large operative unit with no flagged cell anywhere in its 2 by 2 block, jump straight to the POP and leave IsoDrawCtx.nPal at 0 for the caller, which reuses it for the terrain glyphs.
column5: 0x1CA58 (large, after the four bFlags44 tests) and the small path after the re-test at 0x1CA50 both branch to 0x1D5E4, which is ADD SP,SP,#8 / POP {R4-R11,PC}; the restore lives only at 0x1D5DC, LDR R3,[SP,#8+var_4] then STR R3,[R4,#0x6C]

column4: The weapon overlay chooses its object by a fall-through chain: the selected weapon, then a left-hand weapon, then a right-hand weapon, then the left hand's object, then the right hand's object. With BOTH hands empty the last step is LDREQ R3,[R2] with R2 = 0, a null dereference. Nothing in the function tests pHandR before that load.
column5: 0x1D344 loads pHandR and 0x1D34C tests it null and branches straight to 0x1D37C; 0x1D37C is CMP R3,#0 / LDRNE R3,[R3] / LDREQ R3,[R2], and 0x1D388 then reads [R3,#0xA0]

column4: The two-hand weapon offset is read as aUnitFacingDrawOff[2*(8*nUnitType + bFacing)] and that table is 224 bytes: 14 unit types, not 23. A unit of type 14 or above reaching this branch reads past the table into the u16 table at 0xA9488 that Map_TraceVoxelOccupancy (0x3242c) indexes as 4*(8*nUnitType + bFacing).
column5: 0x1D288..0x1D294 is LDRB R2,[R5,#5] / LDRB R3,[R5,#0xA0] / ADD R3,R2,R3,LSL#3 / ADD R3,R0,R3,LSL#1 / LDRSB R3,[R3] with no bound test; aUnitFacingDrawOff ends at 0xA9488

column4: The cell-grid allocator stores the result of operator new(0x3C) whether or not it succeeded, then calls MapCell_Init on the same pointer. MapCell_Init has no null guard, so a failed allocation is a write to address zero.
column5: 0x22EF4 MOV R3,#0x15338 is the store base; the loop stores the new pointer at Map+0x15338 + 4*(60*nY+nX) + 0x3840*nLayer and calls MapCell_Init with it unconditionally; only the MapCell_Reset call is guarded

column4: The tail masks every cell's nFlags32 with 0xFFFFFF87 through the loaded cell pointer with no null test, so one cell the allocator failed to produce is a crash.
column5: 0x25740 MOV R3,#0x15338; the walk loads the cell dword and ANDs [cell+32] with no CMP against zero anywhere in 0x2571C..0x257B0

column4: The craft pad name is aPlane[9*(Map_nMissionType - 1)] with no test for mission type 0, so a type 0 mission reads nine bytes before aPlane, landing in the zero padding between aAlienSecondaryCounts and aHwpsDeployOffsets.
column5: 0x231EC LDR R0,=aPlane with the index formed as 9*Map_nMissionType - 9; aPlane starts at 0xA6668 and aAlienSecondaryCounts ends at 0xA6667

column4: The UFO module name index 3*(Map_nTerrainVariant-1) + Map_nMissionTier is not bounded against the 15-slot aUfo1a: a variant above 5, or a tier above 2, reads past the table into the alien tables. The port yields an empty name instead, which fails the .ma1 load the way a missing member does.
column5: 0x2303C and 0x236DC LDR R3,=aUfo1a; aUfo1a ends at 0xA6617 and aAlienRaceCounts starts at 0xA6618

column4: The loader sizes each block as operator new(2 * (AssetReader_Size() / 2)) and then reads the FULL member size into it, so an odd member overflows the allocation by one byte. It also overwrites the two globals without freeing what the previous load left, so a reload leaks the first pair.
column5: 0x3BDA8 operator new(2*(size/2)) then 0x3BDC0 AssetReader_Read(pBuf, AssetReader_Size()); same pair at 0x3BDF0 / 0x3BE10; neither site frees the old pointer

column4: The layer switch writes var_350 / var_354 only for a layer count of 1, 2 or 3. Zero skips the consumer, but 4 or more reach the showship reveal centre with values this function never wrote.
column5: 0x3CE70 switch on Map_nMapLayers: 1 and 3 store (5,10), 2 stores (5,5), there is no default; var_350 / var_354 are read at 0x3CEA4

column4: When operator new(0x14) for the briefing pad fails, the code stores the prologue's zero register into unk_15692C and calls PadImage_Load anyway; 0x3D2E8 then writes through the stored NULL.
column5: 0x3D2B8 CMP R0,#0 and 0x3D2BC BEQ loc_3D2CC; 0x3D2CC MOV R0,R11 where R11 is the zero set at 0x3C598; 0x3D2E8 STR R11,[R0]

column4: The briefing pad global unk_15692C is overwritten without freeing what the previous mission allocated: with zero on the skip path at 0x3D548, and with the new pad at 0x3D2D0.
column5: 0x3D548 LDR R0,=0x15692C then STR R11,[R0]; 0x3D2D0 STR R0,[R5]; neither site frees the old pointer

column4: AssetReader_Find for showship.dat is not tested, so a missing member leaves the reader size at zero and the code allocates zero bytes that the reveal block then reads its two header words through. The port stores NULL for a zero-size member, which the reveal block already treats as nothing to reveal.
column5: 0x3CADC LDR R1,=aShowshipDat with no test on the AssetReader_Find result; AssetReader_Size feeds operator new; the header words are read at 0x3CEA4

column4: Its first argument is the facility grid the caller wants written, and the function never reads it: every store goes through the global 0x159768. Both callers pass the grid they mean, so the difference is latent.
column5: 0x623BC takes 6 arguments; R0 is overwritten at 0x623C0 by the bClear load and never used, while 0x62428 and 0x624B8 load 0x159768 directly

column4: Nothing bounds nBaseIndex, nX, nY or nFacType. aFacBuildSpec has 18 three-byte records, so a facility type of 18 or more reads past it, and a base index of 8 writes past the 1524-byte grid.
column5: 0x623E8 forms 3*nFacType + aFacBuildSpec with no test; 0x62418 forms 24*nBase + nY with no test

column4: The hangar (type 11) is a 2 by 2 footprint: it marks all four tileA quadrants 9, 10, 11 and 12 but gives build days to only three of them. The ARM reaches the day bytes as +0, +1 and +7 from the anchor, and +7 is the diagonal, so the (nY+1,nX) cell never gets one.
column5: 0x6247C STRB R4,[R5,R3]!; 0x62480 STRB R4,[R5,#1]; 0x62484 STRB R4,[R5,#7] against 0x62438/0x62444/0x62458/0x62460, which do cover all four quadrants

column4: The return value is 6*(24*nBase + nY + 18), the address delta the facType store used. It is register residue, not a status, and no caller uses it.
column5: 0x624F8 MUL R0,R11,R0 with R11 = R7 + 0x12, then POP {R4-R11,PC}

column4: With the grant flag clear the function adds nothing and returns its own first argument, which is otherwise unused; the base it grants to comes from the global at Map+0x1174.
column5: 0x95FA8 MOV R3,R1,LSL#24 / MOVS / BEQ locret_96018; locret_96018 is POP {R4,PC} with R0 unchanged

column4: The hangar scan's second test reads fac[nBase].layer2[1][result+1] -- row 1, always -- while the stamp it authorises goes to layer2[v10+1][result+1]. For any row below the first, the cell that was tested and the cell that is written are different cells.
column5: 0x2CC1C ADD R11,R6,R0 / 0x2CC28 ORR R10,R10,#3 / 0x2CC2C LDRB R11,[R11,R10] with R10 = 0x1C3 and no v10 term, against 0x2CDA0 STRB R2,[R3,#0x4F] which does carry v10

column4: The scan runs v10 and result over 0..4 only, so it searches a 5 by 5 corner of a 6 by 6 grid: a hangar cell in the last row or the last column is never found.
column5: 0x2CC18 CMP R0,#5 and 0x2CCD8 CMP R1,#5 against a 36-byte layer

column4: A craft type outside 0..4 matches the cell and writes Ship.bHangarX and bHangarY, then falls through the switch into the inner loop increment: nothing is stamped, the loop keeps going, and the coordinates from the unmatched match stay written.
column5: 0x2CC9C..0x2CCBC five CMP/BEQ pairs with no default, falling into 0x2CCC0 ADD R0,R0,#1 / CMP R0,#5 / BLT loc_2CC0C

column4: When operator new(0x44) fails the code still stores the NULL into apCraft and still bumps the id and the count; if the scan then matches, 0x2CC8C writes the hangar column through that NULL.
column5: 0x2CB38 CMP R0,#0 / BEQ loc_2CB5C, and loc_2CB5C is MOV R0,#0 into the same store path at 0x2CB7C

column4: The return value is the inner counter: the column index on a match, and 5 when nothing matched. No caller uses it.
column5: 0x2CDA4 is the single return block reached from both the match at 0x2CDA0 and the loop exit at 0x2CCDC, with R0 unchanged

column4: The throw branch tests only bTrajHitStop and then dereferences pArrowThrownItem (Map+0x14070) and its pObj with no null check, so a flag set without a stored item is a crash. The port keeps the same unguarded dereference; no test can cover the null path.
column5: 0x1BDC8 LDRB byte_127A25 / BEQ loc_1C238, then 0x1C1F4 LDR R1,[R5,#0x14070] and 0x1C1F8 LDR R3,[R1] with nothing tested between them

column4: The nudge index 10 * Map.nRowId + n is not bounded. nRowId is the raw aim class id Tact_ComputeAimVector stores at Map+0x14088, so an id above 5 reads past the 64-byte nudge table: ids 6 and 7 land in the second copy of it, higher ids land in the tables after that.
column5: 0x1BD18 MUL R3,R2,#0xA then ADD LR,R3,R1 with no CMP anywhere in 0x1BD10..0x1BD60, and 0x305C0 STR R0,[R4,#0x14088] storing nFlags unclamped

column4: The 64-byte glyph nudge table is stored twice in the image, byte_A9290 for x and byte_A92D0 for y, byte for byte identical. The port keeps one copy and audits both addresses against it.
column5: docs/parity/audit_tables.py compares 0xA9290 and 0xA92D0 against the single g_abArrowGlyphOff, both exact

column4: The return value is whatever register the last branch left. MapView_DrawIsoLayer drops it: it reloads pIso into R0 on the very next instruction. The port returns the number of glyphs drawn instead.
column5: 0x21FC8 BL MapView_DrawUnitFacingArrow followed by 0x21FCC MOV R0,R4

column4: The x/y cell divide (MOVS / ADDMI #0xF / ASR #4) is truncating division, not floor: -17 gives -1, not -2. For v < 0, (v + 15) >> 4 equals v / 16 exactly. The port's helper is named Ball_FloorDiv16 and its comment calls it a floor; the arithmetic is right, the name is not.

column4: Both row editors bound their plain-object repeat loop by nRadarPulseTimer / 10 (0xAC224) -- the radar screen's pulse countdown, which the buy/sell screen neither owns nor initialises. How many units one click of "<" or ">" moves therefore depends on a timer from another screen: a timer of 0 runs the loop once, the 255 the radar click leaves behind runs it 26 times, and the value is re-loaded from the global on every iteration. The same bound governs the buy screen's two quantity controls, BuySellScreen_ValidateCapacity (0x75b88) and BuySellScreen_UpdatePrices (0x75878), so one click there buys or sells between 1 and 26 units. Transfer_MoveOneItem (0x9602c) is the fifth handler on the same bound: one click of the transfer screen's "<" moves between 1 and 26 pending units.

The sell guard breaks out of its repeat loop as soon as the base cannot cover the delta; the buy guard only skips the body and lets the loop keep turning, and the money subtraction panel E aux -= price has no floor, so a row whose pending money is below one unit's price ends up negative and the transaction total can go negative too.

column4: The craft count pass and the craft fill pass disagree about which craft get a row. The count pass at 0x96C94 tests only bHomeBase and Craft_CountSoldiersAboard, while the fill pass at 0x97550 adds Ship.bAtBase (0x06). A craft homed at this base, carrying nobody and currently away is counted but never written, so the list gets one empty row. BuySellScreen_BuildPanels' own count pass at 0x76FB4 does test bAtBase, so the two screens treat the same craft differently.
column5: 0x96C94 (two tests, ++v0) against 0x97550 (three tests, with (*v45)[6] != 0); 0x76FB4 on the sell side has the third test too

column4: The destination overlay's own close branch is unreachable, always. TransferScreen_Draw returns at 0x98224 unless bTransferPanelsBuilt is set, so the overlay path can only run with that byte set. Base_HitTestFacilityStrip gates on bTransferPanelsBuilt @ 0x1870EC -- the same byte TransferScreen_Draw tests at 0x98218 to decide whether to draw its panels -- and the gate overwrites the cursor x with 10 and re-enters the compare chain, so the x range test always misses and the call at 0x98980 always returns nSelectedBaseIdx. 0x989D0 then compares that value with the nSelectedBaseIdx the caller passed in as its second argument (0x93EA8), so the NE at 0x989D4 never fires and byte_1870F8 is never cleared here. The store at 0x98994 has the same cause: with the overlay open the destination base byte_1870F4 is pinned to the source base, so the overlay cannot pick a destination at all. The overlay is closed by the geoscape pointer handlers instead.

column4: The progress column divides BEFORE it multiplies, and ResearchScreen_RefreshPanels does the opposite, so the same topic on the same data shows a different percentage depending on which function last drew it. BuildPanels: 0x73834 LDRH R1,[R10,#0xA] as the dividend, 0x73850 LDRH R0,[R10,#8] as the divisor, _rt_sdiv, then 0x73870 MUL R0,R3,#0x64 on the QUOTIENT -- 100 * (wProgress / wTotal). RefreshPanels: 0x73168 MUL R1,R2,#0x64 on the dividend, then the sdiv at 0x73184 -- (100 * wProgress) / wTotal. A topic one quarter done therefore reads 0% when the panels are built and 25% after any refresh, which is what the player sees when the screen updates under a running topic. Both also divide by wTotal with no test.

The column clear that follows the unlock roll re-clears the FINISHED topic's eight per-base entries instead of the newly unlocked topic's, so a topic can be unlocked while still carrying a stale allocation. ResearchScreen_AccumulateAllocated (0x74914) books auResearchCol[i] into wProgress for every i below the entry count, locked topics included, so the stale entry is not hypothetical.
column5: 0x74428 ADD R7,R3,R7,LSL#1 (R7 = &auResearchCol[nTopic]) / 0x7461C..0x74644 the rolled index (R4 = idx+lo) is used only for the bUnlocked STRB [R3,#9] and the nResearchTopicShown STR [R6,R12] / 0x74648 MOV R0,R7 then eight STRH with ADD R0,#0x120

column4: The panels-not-built half of the buy/sell frame dereferences all five buy/sell panels after BuySellScreen_BuildPanels' teardown has deleted them, and it reads the row marker without subtracting the 2000 alien offset. BuySellScreen_BuildPanels (0x76de0) tears the panels down at 0x77D60..0x77E38 -- UiPanel_FreeLines plus operator delete for A, B, E, C, D -- and never nulls pBuySellPanelA..E; the last thing the teardown does is the funds rollback STRNE at 0x77E50. BuySellScreen_Draw then writes bFlag7073 and bUnk7080 into the freed panels at 0x78864..0x7889C, reads panel B's nLineCount at 0x788E4 for the separator height, reads panel A's aux column at 0x78B54, and at 0x78B80 uses that marker straight as an object index, so an alien row (marker = slot + 2000) would deref apObjects[2077]. The built half does subtract 2000 at 0x784E8, which is what makes the omission here look unintended.

column4: The palette copy that opens the radar screen runs 766 dwords while a palette slot holds 256. The stores cover slot 1 (menu.pal, the intended target) in full, then all 256 entries of slot 2 and 254 of 256 in slot 3; the reads run from slot 26 (all_btn.pal) through slot 27 (ufoflash.pal) and 254 entries of slot 28 (funding.pal). Palette_Load("base.pal", 3) at 0x5FC58 repairs slot 3 immediately, and the close path reloads slot 1 with menu.pal at 0x60290, but nothing anywhere in the binary ever reloads slot 2: from the first radar screen to the end of the session slot 2 holds ufoflash.pal. No Palette_Load in the binary targets slot 2 at all.

column4: The round a shot consumes is gated only on the projectile offset being 0 and on the -1 "unlimited" sentinel. The -2 "no weapon on this mount" sentinel is not exempt. A mount whose id is outside 25..30 -- 24, the psi amplifier, is the one the shipped data uses -- stores a zero weapon range in RadarScreen_DrawCraftArmament, so once the radar's reach falls to 0 the engage byte is set and the cooldown stays at 255 (nothing ever lands, so nothing rearms it downward). The mount's switch in DrawOverlay has no arm for that id, so the projectile offset is never advanced and the "a shot started" test stays true on every frame: the ammo counter walks off through -3, -4, -5 ... without bound, and DrawCraftArmament's label test is `!= -2`, so the radar screen starts drawing the runaway number where an ammo count should be.

column4: The full-zoom exit cannot clear the OTHER craft chasing the same contact. Ship_ClearInterceptByStrategIdx at 0x61434 is reached through BLEQ, so it runs only when the zero flag is set; the only path that arrives with it set is 0x61428 LDRB bRadarTraceLost / 0x6142C LDRBEQ bRadarFlip / 0x61430 ANDSEQ, i.e. bRadarTraceLost == 0 AND bRadarFlip == 0. But the gate that let this block run at all, 0x613BC, already requires bRadarFlip != 0. So when an intercept reaches full zoom with the trace still held, only nInterceptShipIdx is retargeted at 0x613EC and every other craft with bIntercepting set and the same nStrategIdx keeps chasing a contact the radar screen has given up on.

column4: The same sample-to-cell conversion is written two ways in one function. The shot loop multiplies by the double 1/12 and truncates; the three resolve loops truncate the double and integer-divide by 12. 1/12 is not exact in binary, so at a sample height that is an exact multiple of 12 the two land a layer apart - and the muzzle heights the aim setup builds are 12 * nZ + 6, so the case is reachable.

column4: The fire tick's six passes only ever use slot indices 0..3. The WEST and NORTH neighbour passes rewrite R1 to 1 and 2, so they charge the cell's OWN wall A / wall B counter through the same wall sprite. A wall between two burning cells takes double damage and no counter is ever charged from a neighbour's own storage.

column4: A sprite absorbs the hit when bStrength >= counter + step, and bStrength 255 always absorbs it because the term is already zeroed by then. The only counters that ever grow belong to faces with no sprite at all (or bStrength 255 with counter + step above 255).

column4: The burn-run probe multiplies the axis delta by a counter running 0, -1, -2, so it steps AGAINST the run direction: with the west axis it probes east, and the forward pass then starts two cells EAST of the burning cell and walks back over it.
